scope: Application-owned structured operational logs and their correlation metadata; this packet does not govern or replace authoritative account audit, ledger, accounting, or legal records.

dependencyGate.reason: KAN-220 must supply its reviewed prerequisite before this draft can receive an effective decision.

reviewers.requiredDecision: Classify the identifier set and approve least-privilege, audit, break-glass, and incident-response controls.
Approve purpose limitation, actor lookup, evidence handling, deletion, data-subject handling, and legal-hold interaction.
Approve operability of environment separation, access lifecycle, query limits, audit capture, retention, and break-glass revocation.

classificationBasis.reason: Even independently non-secret diagnostic identifiers become linkable customer, security, or financial metadata when joined across events.
prohibitedInputs: raw request, response, header, query, path, or message content
contact, residency, IP, user-agent, wallet, signature, nonce, or provider payload data
raw idempotency keys, chain transaction hashes, amounts, balances, postings, SQL, exceptions, or environment values

actorIdentities.name: initiatorActorId
actorIdentities.meaning: Verified internal account UUID for the principal that initiated the causal work.
actorIdentities.provenance: Authentication principal resolver only; never caller headers, bodies, queries, wallet addresses, or token claims.
actorIdentities.restrictions: May correlate an approved incident case; must never authenticate, authorize, establish tenancy, or make a financial decision.

actorIdentities.name: service-and-workload-executor
actorIdentities.meaning: Fixed service name plus closed runtime workload identifies the software executor, not a person or customer.
actorIdentities.provenance: Logger construction and trusted runtime configuration.
actorIdentities.restrictions: Must not be relabeled as the initiating customer and does not prove the deployed task identity.

actorIdentities.name: durableAuditActor
actorIdentities.meaning: Authoritative actor captured by append-only account or ledger audit records outside the log store.
actorIdentities.restrictions: Operational logs may carry only the allowlisted reference and may never replace, amend, delete, or satisfy retention for the durable audit record.

correlationFields.name: correlationId
correlationFields.source: Server-generated canonical UUIDv4 root, or a legacy namespace-separated SHA-256 diagnostic value for a normalized legacy envelope.
correlationFields.emission: Any catalog event emitted while a causal context is active, including trace.span.completed.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Follow one causal chain across API, outbox, queue, worker, and ledger events.

correlationFields.name: requestId
correlationFields.source: Server-generated ingress UUIDv4 equal to the root correlationId.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Locate the server-generated request returned to a caller and pivot to its root correlation.

correlationFields.name: initiatorActorId
correlationFields.source: Verified internal account principal bound after authentication.
correlationFields.emission: Context-bearing catalog events except trace.span.completed; absent for anonymous or failed authentication.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Security- or Privacy-approved investigation of activity attributed to one internal account.

correlationFields.name: jobId
correlationFields.source: Domain-separated SHA-256 diagnostic projection of an internal job identifier.
correlationFields.emission: Validated context-bearing events except trace.span.completed, and the exact job catalog events that permit jobId.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Follow one normalized durable job without disclosing its raw transport identifier.

correlationFields.name: messageId
correlationFields.source: Domain-separated SHA-256 diagnostic projection of a transport message identifier.
correlationFields.emission: Only job.published, job.processed, job.retry_scheduled, job.awaiting_dead_letter, and job.ownership_lost.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Distinguish transport attempts and redeliveries without exposing the raw provider identifier.

correlationFields.name: intentId
correlationFields.source: Validated internal intent UUID when a real domain producer exists.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Follow an approved internal intent workflow after its domain contract and privacy purpose are reviewed.

correlationFields.name: quoteId
correlationFields.source: Validated internal quote UUID when a real domain producer exists.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Follow an approved internal quote workflow after its domain contract and privacy purpose are reviewed.

correlationFields.name: transactionId
correlationFields.allowedUse: Pivot from an operational incident to the separately authorized authoritative ledger query.

correlationFields.name: ledgerEventId
correlationFields.allowedUse: Pivot from an operational incident to the separately authorized immutable journal or event record.

correlationFields.name: traceId
correlationFields.source: Domain-separated SHA-256 projection of the server-authoritative root correlation.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Assemble the bounded application trace graph for an approved incident.

correlationFields.name: spanId
correlationFields.allowedUse: Identify one bounded span inside an approved trace reconstruction.

correlationFields.name: parentSpanId
correlationFields.source: Validated nonzero parent application span identifier distinct from spanId.
correlationFields.allowedUse: Reconstruct parent-child relationships inside an approved trace.

environmentSeparation: Development, test, staging, and production use distinct log groups, encryption keys, reader roles, and evidence locations.
A grant names one environment and exact service log groups; wildcard groups, cross-environment readers, and developer production inheritance are forbidden.
Production query access uses workforce identity with phishing-resistant MFA, short sessions, and no shared identities; implementation evidence remains pending.
Application runtime roles can append only to their own environment and workload log group and cannot read, query, export, change retention, or delete.
auditRequirements: Record grant, denial, query, export request, retention change, deletion, hold, release, break-glass activation, and revocation in an access-controlled administrative audit store separate from application logs.

Capture workforce principal, assumed role, case or change reference, environment, exact groups, UTC range, projected fields, query-template identifier, one-way parameter fingerprint, result count and bytes, timestamps, outcome, and approving roles without copying raw result values into the audit event.
Deny query execution when the administrative audit record cannot be created, except the declared break-glass procedure; break-glass must spool tamper-evident local metadata for later ingestion.
The application log writer must have no capability to alter the administrative access audit trail.

breakGlass.trigger: Declared severity-one incident where delay creates material customer, security, or financial harm and the normal incident role is unavailable or insufficient.
breakGlass.authorization: Incident commander plus Security approver before activation when feasible; otherwise one authorized commander with mandatory retrospective Security and Privacy review.
breakGlass.scope: One workforce principal, one environment, exact log groups, read and bounded query only.
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA and a fresh short-lived session.
No shared account, persistent key, wildcard group, silent export, deletion, retention change, or hold action.
Notify Security and Operations at activation; record all queries and results metadata.
Revoke automatically at expiry or incident handoff, whichever occurs first.
Complete access and privacy review within one business day and track every exception to closure.

retentionAndDeletion.rule: Fourteen days is the proposed standard for managed application log groups. Any other allowlisted value requires a pre-deployment, environment-specific exception with purpose, cost, privacy, owner, and expiry review.
retentionAndDeletion.localEvidence: Test-captured output is process- or test-artifact-bound, contains synthetic identifiers only, and is deleted under the local test artifact lifecycle rather than uploaded.
retentionAndDeletion.normalDeletion: Backend expiry deletes application log events after the approved period. Manual deletion is forbidden except an approved contamination, legal, or platform-response procedure executed by the configuration administrator and independently audited.
retentionAndDeletion.dataSubjectHandling: Privacy determines whether an internal actor lookup is lawful and responsive. Search and evidence must be minimized; deletion must not be promised where a legal duty, hold, or authoritative financial-record rule applies.

legalHold.rule: Do not silently extend a whole log group or disable expiry. Export only the case-minimum result set to an approved restricted evidence store, record source groups and UTC bounds, compute an integrity digest, apply a case schedule, and keep source expiry unchanged unless Legal, Privacy, Security, Records, and Operations approve an explicit time-bound exception.
legalHold.release: The Records custodian releases the case hold under documented Legal authority, records disposition evidence, and leaves authoritative financial/audit schedules unchanged.

immutableFinancialRecordBoundary: Application logs are diagnostic copies and never the book of record, an account audit record, proof of authorization, or a substitute for ledger retention.
A transactionId or ledgerEventId is only a pivot to a separately authorized authoritative query; log content cannot establish balance, amount, posting, finality, ownership, or approval.

Log expiry, deletion, contamination response, export, hold, or hold release must never update, erase, rewrite, truncate, or relax append-only controls on account audit, journal, posting, lifecycle, outbox, reconciliation, or approval records.
Financial corrections remain append-only reversal or compensation records under ledger policy; a log record may not be used to mutate history.

authorizedUseCases.purpose: Trace one reported request or causal workflow to diagnose an active incident.
Investigate suspected account compromise, authorization failure, or abuse under a Security case and Privacy-approved purpose.
Locate operational failures around a known immutable financial record without treating logs as financial evidence.
Identify a service-wide operational failure when no correlation identifier is yet known.
Collect a minimized result set under documented Legal or Privacy authority and an approved evidence-handling plan.

prohibitedUses: Curiosity, employee performance review, marketing, product analytics, customer segmentation, or bulk behavior profiling.
Discovery by raw wallet address, contact detail, IP address, token claim, request content, amount, balance, posting, chain hash, provider payload, or other prohibited field.
Unbounded scans, cross-environment joins, unrestricted exports, or searching for credentials and then copying a discovered value.
Authentication, authorization, tenancy, balance calculation, accounting, transaction finality, or any financial decision based on log content.

minimumFilters.actorProjectionRule: initiatorActorId is excluded by default and may be selected or searched only for SECURITY_ACCOUNT_ACTIVITY or LEGAL_PRIVACY_CASE with a documented Privacy purpose.
minimumFilters.financialProjectionRule: transactionId and ledgerEventId may be selected only for FINANCIAL_WORKFLOW_DIAGNOSIS or LEGAL_PRIVACY_CASE and only as pivots to an authorized source-of-record query.

evidenceHandling: Inspect in the approved query interface; do not paste results or restricted identifiers into Jira, chat, email, source control, terminal history, or ordinary screenshots.
Export only when the use case requires evidence and a second authorized role approves the exact fields, rows, destination, retention, and custodian.
Use a restricted case identifier for filenames; encrypt in transit and at rest; record byte count and SHA-256; never include credentials or prohibited content in the evidence manifest.
Redact nonessential identifiers from reports, preserve original evidence only in the approved store, and record access, transfer, hold, and disposition.
If prohibited material appears, stop querying and copying, preserve only safe metadata, notify Security and Privacy, contain the producer or sink, and use the separate incident process.
escalation: Obtain Security and Privacy approval before actor-based lookup, scope beyond the initial bounds, cross-service expansion not linked by a root correlation, or evidence export.
Obtain Operations approval before a query exceeds twenty-four hours, accesses another environment, or materially increases scanned volume or cost.
Escalate any suspected financial discrepancy to the Ledger, Finance, and Records owners for an authoritative database audit; do not broaden log authority.
Use break-glass only for its declared trigger and revoke it at expiry; it cannot authorize deletion, retention changes, financial mutation, or an otherwise prohibited search.

owners.control: classification, access model, security incident use, and break-glass
purpose limitation, actor lookup, data-subject handling, evidence minimization, and privacy incidents
log groups, identity lifecycle, environment separation, retention execution, query tooling, and audit collection
financial-record boundary, legal hold, evidence schedule, and disposition

cadence: Operations reviews production and non-production access membership at least quarterly; Security and Privacy attest or remediate the review.
Security samples query, denial, export, and break-glass audit records monthly; Privacy joins when actor lookup or customer evidence occurred.
Operations verifies retention, deletion, environment separation, and audit delivery at least quarterly in an explicitly authorized environment.
Security, Privacy, Operations, Records, and Finance review this policy at least annually and after every material incident or exception.
exceptionRequirements: Name the control, business and incident purpose, exact fields, environment, groups, principals, start, expiry, compensating controls, cost bound, evidence destination, and accountable owner.
Obtain Security, Privacy, and Operations decisions before activation; add Legal, Records, and Finance when retention, hold, or financial evidence is affected.
Expire automatically in at most thirty days unless a shorter access or break-glass bound applies; renewal is a new review.
Never authorize a prohibited input, shared identity, logs as financial authority, or mutation/deletion of immutable financial records.
reReviewTriggers: Any new or renamed structured event, correlation field, actor source, identifier format, event-field mapping, logger schema version, or legacy enrichment path.
Any new log sink, query backend, exporter, dashboard, alert, subprocessor, Region, encryption key, environment topology, or cross-account access path.
Any change to retention, deletion, backup, legal hold, data-subject process, cost model, or evidence destination.
Any authentication, authorization, tenancy, ledger, outbox, reconciliation, or financial-record change that alters identifier meaning or authority.
Any leak, unauthorized query, failed audit capture, break-glass use, material access-review finding, or regulatory/contractual change.
Resolution or material change of KAN-220, KAN-49, KAN-50, KAN-51, or KAN-52.

unresolvedGates: KAN-220 is still TO_DO and must complete with reviewed prerequisite output.
Security has not approved actor and identifier classification, access, audit, query, or break-glass controls.
Privacy has not approved purpose limitation, actor lookup, data-subject handling, evidence minimization, deletion, or legal-hold interaction.
Operations has not approved or implemented environment-separated roles, administrative audit capture, retention/deletion procedures, query templates, break-glass activation, or revocation.
Legal, Records, and Finance have not approved the legal-hold/evidence schedule or confirmed the immutable financial-record boundary for this use.
No merged-commit, tree, packet, or logger-contract hashes are bound to an independent decision.
No authorized non-production exercise proves effective delivery, encryption, access denial, query auditability, expiry, deletion, hold, or break-glass behavior.
